question: An object of size 1.0 cm is placed in front of a concave mirror of focal length 16 cm, at a distance of 24 cm. The image formed is ______ and its height is ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**inverted, 2.0 cm**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The image formed by a concave mirror when the object is placed between the focal point and the center of curvature is **inverted and real**.
 
• **Given**:
 
 
• Focal Length f=-16cm (Negative for concave mirror)
 
• Object distance u=-24cm (Negative for objects in front of the mirror)
 
• Object size h_o=1cm
 
 
 
• Step 1: Use the mirror formula to find the image distance v.
 
 
• The mirror formula is: (1)/(f)=(1)/(v)+(1)/(u)
 
• Substitute the given values: (1)/(-16)=(1)/(v)+(1)/(-24)
 
• Rightarrow (-3+2)/(48)=(1)/(v)
 
• Rightarrow -(1)/(48)=(1)/(v)
 
• Thus: v=-28cm
 
 
 
• Step 2: Use the magnification formula to find the image height hᵢ.​
 
 
• The magnification m=(h_i)/(h_o)=(v)/(u)
 
• Substitute the known values: m=(-48)/(-24)=2
 
• Now, calculate the image height: h_i = m × h_o = 2 × 1.0 cm = 2.0 cm
 
 
 
• Final Answer:
 
 
• **The image formed is real and inverted.**
 
• **The height of the image is 2.0 cm.**
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror with an inward-curved reflective surface.
 
• It can form both real and virtual images depending on the position of the object relative to the focal point and the center of curvature.
 
• Real images formed by concave mirrors are inverted, and virtual images are erect.
 
• Concave mirrors are used in applications such as telescopes, shaving mirrors, and headlights due to their ability to converge light.
